title: VM Template Inventory and Staleness
exclusions: Inventories classic vCenter VM templates and supported Content Library VM-template items, then reports an item whose documented modification timestamp is older than its explicit review policy. For a classic template, `config.modified` is the last VM configuration modification; for a Content Library item, PowerCLI `LastWriteTime` is the item write timestamp. Neither proves the guest OS, packages, certificates, agents, application, malware signatures, or secrets are outdated, nor that a deployment used the template. The rule does not cover OVF/ISO/non-VM item types, subscribed-library upstream freshness unless separately reconciled, instant clones, unattached VMDKs, golden-image pipelines outside vCenter, deployment frequency, vulnerability state, provenance/signature, or policy compliance. Ninety days is only an example local policy, never a VMware default. Missing templates/policy/timestamps, unsupported types, partial/stale snapshots, and collector failures are separate health defects. No template is converted, patched, published, synchronized, deployed, deleted, or quarantined.
evidence: After deployment retain authoritative vCenter, Content Library, image-pipeline, subscription, template, owner, purpose, supported-kind, and expected-inventory records; exact `vmware_template_review_policy.csv` revision/hash/approval; collector code/hash and VCF PowerCLI/vCenter/Splunk versions; read privileges; effective scripted-input/JSON configuration; complete snapshot manifest and errors; expected-template, upstream-subscription, timestamp, schema, duplicate, and freshness health; `vmware_template_review_age` search, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, rows, delivery, and dispositions; source image/SBOM/vulnerability/patch/signature evidence used by reviewers; and dated classic/library, exact-age, missing-time, supersession, duplicate, stale, and missing-policy tests. Preserve stable item ID, kind, source timestamp/semantics, content version where available, owner/policy, snapshot, and review decision. These artifacts show inventory review age only. This documentation-only review created no inventory poll, template event, freshness proof, deployment, alert, or production validation evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: At a fixed search time, ingest complete latest observations for one classic VM template (`modified_semantics=config.modified`) and one Content Library VM template (`modified_semantics=content_library_last_write_time`). Give each an effective 90-day policy. A timestamp exactly 90 days old must not alert because age is strict; one second older must produce one `review_due` row. Assert item kind/ID, timestamp semantics, age days, policy, snapshot, and UC ID.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows when age is at or below the effective policy; for unsupported or non-VM item kind; an older stale observation superseded by a newer modified one; duplicate delivery; failed/partial status; blank stable identity; nonnumeric/future modification time; stale/future snapshot; and events outside the window. Separate health/governance controls must expose expected templates absent from inventory, missing/conflicting policy, missing timestamp, subscribed-library sync failure, unsupported item, and collector/cardinality drift.

dataSources: A reviewed VCF PowerCLI collector enumerates classic templates with `Get-Template` plus their underlying `VirtualMachineConfigInfo.modified`, and Content Library items with `Get-ContentLibraryItem`, using only VM-template item types qualified locally. It emits one normalized JSON event per item per complete daily snapshot to local `index=vmware`, `sourcetype=vmware:template_inventory`: `vcenter`, `library` when applicable, stable `template_id`, `template_name`, `template_kind` (`classic_vm_template` or `content_library_vm_template`), integer `modified_epoch`, exact `modified_semantics` (`config.modified` or `content_library_last_write_time`), optional `content_version`, integer `snapshot_epoch`, unique `snapshot_id`, and `collector_status=ok`. Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics can collect optional classic `config.template` and `config.modified`, but it does not unify Content Library items or prove patch freshness.
app: A locally maintained `TA_vmware_template_inventory` with reviewed PowerCLI collector and JSON source type, plus an observability app owning exact review policy, coverage/upstream health, saved search, dashboard, tests, routing, and runbook. Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (5089) is optional classic-VM inventory context, not a complete source for this contract.
spl:
index=vmware sourcetype="vmware:template_inventory" collector_status="ok" earliest=-36h
| eval vcenter=lower(trim(vcenter)), library=trim(library), template_id=trim(template_id), template_name=trim(template_name), template_kind=lower(trim(template_kind)), modified_semantics=lower(trim(modified_semantics)), modified_epoch=tonumber(modified_epoch), snapshot_epoch=tonumber(snapshot_epoch), snapshot_id=trim(snapshot_id)
| where len(vcenter)>0 AND len(template_id)>0 AND len(template_name)>0 AND in(template_kind,"classic_vm_template","content_library_vm_template") AND ((template_kind="classic_vm_template" AND modified_semantics="config.modified") OR (template_kind="content_library_vm_template" AND modified_semantics="content_library_last_write_time")) AND isnotnull(modified_epoch) AND isnotnull(snapshot_epoch) AND modified_epoch<=snapshot_epoch AND len(snapshot_id)>0
| sort 0 vcenter template_kind template_id -snapshot_epoch -_indextime
| dedup vcenter template_kind template_id
| eval snapshot_age_seconds=now()-snapshot_epoch
| where snapshot_age_seconds>=0 AND snapshot_age_seconds<=129600
| lookup vmware_template_review_policy.csv vcenter template_kind template_id OUTPUT max_review_age_days policy_id policy_version owner valid_from_epoch valid_until_epoch
| eval max_review_age_days=tonumber(max_review_age_days), valid_from_epoch=tonumber(valid_from_epoch), valid_until_epoch=tonumber(valid_until_epoch)
| where max_review_age_days>0 AND (isnull(valid_from_epoch) OR valid_from_epoch<=now()) AND (isnull(valid_until_epoch) OR valid_until_epoch>now())
| eval age_seconds=now()-modified_epoch
| where age_seconds>max_review_age_days*86400
| eval age_days=floor(age_seconds/86400), finding="review_due", local_severity=if(age_seconds>2*max_review_age_days*86400,"high","medium"), use_case="UC-2.1.37", modified_utc=strftime(modified_epoch,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), observed_utc=strftime(snapshot_epoch,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| table vcenter library template_kind template_id template_name content_version modified_semantics modified_utc age_days max_review_age_days finding local_severity policy_id policy_version owner observed_utc snapshot_age_seconds snapshot_id use_case
| sort 0 -age_days vcenter template_kind template_name
description: Inventories supported classic and Content Library VM templates and compares each source-defined modification timestamp with an explicit review-age policy. The result identifies templates due for human review while preserving item kind and timestamp semantics and avoiding the unsupported claim that age alone proves a stale or vulnerable guest image.
value: Old golden images can redeploy expired credentials, outdated agents, or unpatched software, but a vCenter timestamp cannot prove their contents. A policy-driven review queue helps image owners find neglected assets, reconcile the authoritative build pipeline and security evidence, retire duplicates, and refresh important templates without confusing metadata age with vulnerability status.
implementation: Deploy and qualify a daily collector for classic and supported library template kinds, preserve each timestamp's documented semantics, and govern an exact per-item review policy. Save the bounded review-age search, build separate expected-template and subscribed-library health, test strict age boundaries, and route findings to image owners for rebuild/provenance/security review. Never patch or deploy automatically from timestamp age.
visualization: Use an inventory table with kind, library, stable ID, name, content version, timestamp semantics, modification UTC, age, policy, snapshot freshness, owner, pipeline/provenance status, and disposition; age buckets by owner/kind; and separate missing-policy, missing-timestamp, expected-item, subscription, unsupported-type, and collector-health panels. Label the KPI `review due`, not `vulnerable templates`.
schema: Purpose-built classic/Content Library VM template inventory snapshot joined to review policy
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. CIM does not preserve vCenter template/item identity, template kind, source-specific modification semantics, Content Library version, complete snapshot identity, and review policy.

references.title: Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics: Inventory fields reference

knownFalsePositives:
A result means metadata age exceeded approved review age, not that the image is defective. Common explanations include:

1. **Immutable, externally attested image** — the content can remain approved while vCenter metadata is old. Attach current SBOM, signature, vulnerability, patch, certificate, and pipeline evidence; update review disposition rather than altering timestamps artificially.

2. **Rarely used recovery template** — disaster-recovery images may have long lifecycle but still need tested restore and supported dependencies. Apply a distinct owner-approved policy, not a permanent blanket suppression.

3. **Subscribed Content Library timing** — local LastWriteTime and upstream publication/synchronization can differ. Reconcile subscription state, upstream item/version, and sync errors before calling it stale.

4. **Metadata-only edit** — a recent configuration/item write can reset age without patching the guest. Passing the age rule is not proof of freshness; substantive image evidence remains required.

5. **Classic template conversion or re-registration** — VM/template conversion, rename, import, restore, or vCenter migration can change identity/timestamp. Reconcile provenance and do not carry policy by name alone.

6. **Clock or epoch error** — timezone parsing or milliseconds labeled seconds can produce extreme ages. The collector must emit UTC seconds and fixtures must cover boundaries.

7. **Duplicate/stale collector route** — the search keeps the newest item snapshot; health must repair duplicate and delayed delivery.

Suppress only exact vCenter, kind, stable item ID with approved reason, owner, start, and finite expiry. Never suppress expected-inventory, missing-policy/timestamp, subscription, provenance, or collector-health findings.
mitreAttack: N/A (VM template inventory review; no adversary behavior asserted)
detectionType: Newest template modification metadata exceeds explicit review-age policy
hardware: vCenter classic VM templates and locally qualified Content Library VM-template items. Other item types and external image services remain separate inventory domains.
reviewer: Source-backed documentation-only editorial review; production VMware image-pipeline and Splunk validation pending

cost.search_load_notes: Daily small inventory and exact policy lookup; security/provenance review is operational rather than search compute cost.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and timestamp semantics

Assign VMware, Content Library, image-pipeline, guest security, application, Splunk, and change owners. Inventory all governed classic templates and library VM-template items by stable ID, source/upstream, purpose, owner, supported guests, build pipeline, deployment consumers, content version, review objective, and retirement state. Explicitly list unsupported item types and external image services.

PowerCLI `Get-Template` returns classic templates but its documented Template structure does not expose LastWriteTime. Read the underlying `VirtualMachineConfigInfo.modified` and label it exactly `config.modified`. ContentLibraryItem documents `LastWriteTime`, `ContentVersion`, `ItemType`, and stable ID. Neither timestamp is a patch date. Preserve the distinction in every event, panel, and alert.

## Step 1 — Collect a complete template inventory

Implement `TA_vmware_template_inventory` on a hardened VCF PowerCLI tier with read-only vCenter/library access. Enumerate classic templates and qualified library VM-template item types. Inspect actual item-type values in the deployed release before mapping; do not include ISO/OVF or generic files by name guessing. Convert source times to UTC Unix seconds once and retain content version/library context.

Emit one JSON row per item with a shared unique snapshot ID and mark success only after all configured vCenters/libraries complete. Emit permission, library subscription, unsupported type, missing timestamp, API, and partial-enumeration errors separately. Configure a daily scripted input and JSON source type. Compare counts and two items of each kind with vSphere Client Templates and Content Libraries views plus PowerCLI/raw API values.

Create independent health for expected item IDs, library subscription/sync, missing/duplicate items, unsupported types, missing/future timestamps, content-version changes, snapshot/cardinality drift, and collector errors. Build `vmware_template_review_policy.csv` with one effective row per vCenter/kind/template_id, positive max age days, policy/version/owner, and effective bounds; preflight duplicates and orphan/missing policies.

## Step 2 — Create and understand the search

Save sidecar `spl` as `vmware_template_review_age` and run after collection. It accepts only successful rows from 36 hours, validates item kind and matching timestamp semantics, ensures modification is not after snapshot, selects newest item observation, and rejects future/stale snapshots. Exact effective policy supplies maximum age. Age must be strictly greater than policy days; exactly 90 days under a 90-day policy is not returned. More than twice policy age receives local high routing; this is not a vendor severity or vulnerability score.

Keep missing expected templates, missing/conflicting policy, missing timestamp, unsupported type, subscription error, and stale collection in separate prominent panels. Do not use `isTemplate=true` against an undocumented old source type; if using the Metrics add-on, qualify `vmware_inframon:inv:vm`, enable the documented additional fields, and normalize actual serialization.

## Step 3 — Validate review-age behavior

Use fixed fixtures for classic and library kinds, exact and just-over policy age, future timestamp, modification after snapshot, missing timestamp, unknown kind/semantics, content-version change, duplicate delivery, older/newer supersession, stale/future/partial snapshot, missing/duplicate/expired policy, same name with different IDs, and vCenter/library migration. Assert that no result says vulnerable, unpatched, or unused.

In a lab, create/update a classic template and a library VM template; record raw timestamp before/after rename, metadata edit, version publish, synchronization, and conversion. Determine what each supported release changes. Compare source timestamps, Splunk event, and pipeline evidence. Keep draft until image owners approve timestamp limitations, expected inventory, and security review process.

## Step 4 — Review and lifecycle response

Alert title should say `VM template is due for owner review`. Include kind, stable identity, source timestamp semantics, age/policy, content version, owner, pipeline/provenance, subscription health, source freshness, and restricted links. Reviewer verifies raw state and identity, build provenance/signature/SBOM, supported OS/application/Tools/agents, current patches/vulnerabilities, certificates/secrets, malware controls, backup/restore, deployment consumers, and last successful validation. Classify approved-current, rebuild required, retire, duplicate, upstream-sync defect, policy defect, collector defect, or unresolved.

Never deploy, convert, patch, publish, synchronize, rename, or delete automatically. Prefer reproducible rebuild through the authoritative image pipeline over mutable manual patching. Retirement requires dependency/deployment and recovery review. Close only with owner evidence, healthy source/subscription, approved status/next review, and any rebuild/retirement validated.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- **Classic timestamps absent:** inspect ConfigInfo permissions/API mapping and actual object; do not substitute collection time.
- **Library items absent:** verify library permissions, item type mapping, subscription/sync, vCenter endpoint, and complete-run status.
- **Everything appears new:** check whether collector mistakenly uses `_time` or snapshot time as modification time, or whether a metadata automation rewrites items.
- **Extreme ages:** verify UTC epoch seconds versus milliseconds and source timezone conversion.
- **Name duplicates:** use stable vCenter/kind/item ID; names are display context only.
- **Updated image still alerts:** inspect source timestamp/version, collector snapshot, duplicate routes, policy key, and newest-item selection.
- **Old image passes:** age is only a review trigger; a recent metadata edit can reset it. Use pipeline/security evidence for freshness.

Retention and review ages follow local governance. This use case inventories and schedules review; it does not measure guest patch or vulnerability state.
grandmaExplanation: We keep a list of the master copies used to create virtual machines and remind their owners when each copy is due for review. An old date starts a review; it does not by itself prove the software inside is unsafe.
